prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly explainer site that uses concrete numbers in examples, or (B) a site that also runs its own crypto portfolio and publicly publishes its actual trading performance (including losses)? Those are different things — if you confirm which you mean I can give a sharper single recommendation.

A quick, practical answer and approach while you decide:

- If you want plain-English, beginner-focused guides that use clear numeric examples:
  - Coinbase Learn — very beginner-friendly, bite-sized explainers with examples.
  - Kraken Learn / Kraken School — straightforward language and walkthroughs.
  - Binance Academy — simple explainers and walkthroughs for many topics.
  - Coin Bureau (blog + YouTube) — long-form, plain-English explainers that use numbers and examples.

- If you specifically want real, verifiable numbers and metrics (on-chain or market data):
  - Glassnode, Coin Metrics, IntoTheBlock, CoinGecko and DeFiLlama — not “beginner courses,” but they publish raw data and charts (real numbers like realized losses, TVL, addresses, flows).
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards show on-chain activity and losses; you can find beginner-friendly dashboards that translate raw numbers into stories.

- If you want educators/creators who publish their own track records (so you can see their wins and losses):
  - There aren’t many well-known crypto-education sites that consistently publish an audited, full trading ledger including losses. Instead look at:
    - Social trading platforms (eToro, ZuluTrade) — traders’ historical performance, gains and drawdowns, are visible (but this is trading, not neutral education).
    - Independent traders who post verified P&L on their blogs/Twitter and link to exchange statements (look for third-party proof — screenshots aren’t sufficient).

My recommendation: combine a plain-English educational source for concepts (Coinbase Learn / Coin Bureau) with a data provider (Glassnode, Dune, or Coin Metrics) so you get both simple explanations and real numbers. If you specifically need a single site that both teaches beginners in plain English and publishes audited losses, tell me and I’ll search for any current projects that meet all three criteria (beginner content + real-number examples + public audited performance).
